items.t: Urban Meyer Shares True Feelings on Mike Norvell After Florida State Firing: “Go Enjoy Your Family”
sum: Mike Norvell's time at Florida State ended with a familiar feeling for Seminoles fans. Another disappointing Saturday, another loss, and eventually, another coaching change. But while the university decided it had seen enough, Urban Meyer has the best regards for the fired coach.

Speaking on The Triple Option, former national champion coach turned analyst Urban Meyer offered a sympathetic reaction. Having walked away from high-pressure coaching jobs himself, Meyer suggested the 45-year-old coach might be better off stepping away from the chaos to spend time with his family.
"I'm actually happy for the guy," he said. "I'm going to call him at some point this week and move on, go enjoy your family. You made some money there."

Both Rob Stone and Mark Ingram highlighted the staggering buyout number. According to USA TODAY Sports' John Brice, Mike Norvell is owed approximately $50.3 million if fired without cause. That figure would make his payout the third-largest in college football history, behind the settlements involving Jimbo Fisher at Texas A&M and Brian Kelly at LSU.

There was no lengthy lecture about winning football games or a list of mistakes Mike Norvell needed to correct. Urban Meyer seemed to recognize something bigger happening inside the modern college game. And Florida State's recent struggles offered a good example.
Urban Meyer wasn't pretending Mike Norvell's firing came out of nowhere. In fact, he believes the problems had been building for quite some time.

"I mean, it's been coming for three years," the former Ohio State coach added. "The culture just is constantly shifting when you're having this many players come in every year. You know, you have 40 or 50 every year coming in, Mark. I can't even fathom that. You better pick the right ones, man. And your staff better do a great job developing them."

NTU student, 22, owns Mercedes-Benz as first car, credits businesses for success, Singapore News
sum: At just 22, Nanyang Technological University (NTU) student Rayyan Afiq, better known as Rayyan Roulette, already owns a Mercedes-Benz as his first car.
The makeup influencer, who is active on TikTok and Instagram, previously studied Mass Communication at Ngee Ann Polytechnic before pursuing a business degree at NTU.
In a recent episode of Booty Call, hosted by Class 95 DJs The Muttons, Rayyan was asked how someone his age could afford a Mercedes-Benz i, 8days reported on Wednesday (Nov 4).
"Wah! I think it's because I started being on social media when I was really young. Throughout my journey, I also started a few companies that thankfully were profitable," he explained.
Checks by AsiaOne online showed that Rayyan is a co-founder of AIKO Collective, which provides social media marketing, content creation, public relations and talent management services.
"I only talk about the businesses that were successful, but I started so many that failed as well," he shared.
He also credited his mother for encouraging him to explore entrepreneurship while young, recalling her advice to try different things until finding something that works.

Mercedes-Benz Korea Pushed 3,500 Cars onto Dealers After Direct Sales Shift
sum: Mercedes-Benz Korea has sold more than 3,500 vehicles to its dealers, nominally for showroom display and other uses, since introducing a direct sales model in April. Dealers, already running losses in the tens of billions of won, say they are being forced to absorb depreciation costs because of a push to offload inventory so the importer can hit its annual sales target. Mercedes-Benz Korea counters that dealer purchases rose unavoidably because of a heavy slate of new model launches, including the S-Class.

According to imported car industry sources on the 5th, dealers bought more than 3,500 vehicles for their own use, rather than delivering them to customers, during the six months from May to October after Mercedes-Benz Korea rolled out Retail of the Future (RoF), a scheme under which the importer sells cars directly rather than through dealers.

That is more than 12% of the 29,335 vehicles Mercedes-Benz Korea sold in South Korea over the period. In August alone, dealer purchases topped 970 units, close to 25% of the 4,037 vehicles sold that month. Dealer purchases came to about 800 units in September and around 590 last month.

The stated purposes for the purchases were demonstration cars and loaner vehicles. Demonstration cars are displayed at Mercedes-Benz Korea showrooms or used for test drives, while loaner vehicles are lent to customers whose cars are in for repairs.

Dealers contend that Mercedes-Benz Korea is strong-arming them into buying cars so it can meet its annual sales target. Without the dealer purchases, the importer would in practice have had no chance of reaching this year's goal. Its internal target is 62,000 units, and with 49,993 sold from January through October, it would need to sell more than 6,000 vehicles in each of the remaining two months just to scrape by. Had dealers not bought the cars, even that possibility would not have existed.

The 12% share of dealer self-purchases is highly unusual compared with other imported car brands, industry analysis suggests. At BMW and Audi, vehicles sold for display and similar purposes account for about 6% of total sales. "We understand that Mercedes-Benz Korea also has a 6% share as an internal guideline," an official in the dealer industry said.

Mercedes-Benz Share Price Gain Masks a Deeper Earnings Question
sum: A 2.2% rise in the share price is doing a lot of work for Mercedes-Benz investors this week — perhaps more than the underlying numbers can support. The advance came as the company met institutional investors at Jefferies' virtual Asia conference, part of its quarterly roadshow circuit. But the day's move sits awkwardly beside a stream of softer guidance and trimmed valuations, and the gap between the two is where the real investment debate now lies.

On 28 October, Mercedes-Benz reported a 15% decline in adjusted group EBIT for the third quarter of 2026, down to EUR 1.78 billion. That the figure edged past analyst expectations offers only limited comfort. A modest beat against lowered forecasts is not the same as an improvement on the prior year, and investors would do well to keep the distinction sharp: a rising share price is not evidence that the business is getting better.

The more telling signal came roughly a week earlier, when the carmaker cut its expected adjusted return on sales for Mercedes-Benz Cars to 2% to 3% for 2026, down from a previous 3% to 5%. Group EBIT is now guided to land at the prior-year level. Management pointed to a difficult market environment in China and higher anticipated costs in the final quarter, including elevated material expenses.

Those pressures arrive from two directions at once. Even if one front stabilises, continued deterioration on the other could leave the group exposed — and a slightly better-than-feared quarter would offer little protection against a fresh round of expectation cuts.

Operating profit tells only half the story. Free cash flow from the industrial business reached EUR 3.1 billion across the first nine months of 2026, but the third quarter alone contributed just EUR 172 million. For the full year, Mercedes-Benz expects industrial free cash flow well below the prior-year figure.

That combination — a profit line that narrowly cleared the bar and a cash line that thinned out — is why the recovery case cannot rest on earnings alone. What would actually shift the argument is evidence that profit and cash flow are stabilising together. A single encouraging quarter does not clear the uncertainty; a genuine turn in industrial cash generation would carry far more weight.

Zalando shares fall 5% as Q3 margin miss outweighs sales beat
sum: Investing.com -- Shares in Zalando fell more than 5% on Tuesday as a sharper-than-expected decline in third-quarter gross margin overshadowed better-than-expected GMV and revenue growth at the German online fashion retailer, which increased price investments in its consumer business.
The German online fashion retailer's GMV rose 7.5% to €4.54 billion from €4.22 billion a year earlier, beating the% consensus compiled by analysts.
Revenue increased 5.1% to €3.18 billion from €3.02 billion, above expectations for 4.4% growth.
Business-to-consumer revenue rose 2.8% to €2.83 billion, while business-to-business revenue surged 27.9% to €354.40 million.

Gross margin fell 90 basis points year-on-year to 38.7%, missing the 39.9% consensus, as Zalando increased targeted price investments in its consumer business. Margin was also weighed down by the faster growth of its business-to-business operations.

Group EBIT increased 10.6% to €106.50 million from €96.30 million a year earlier, in line with expectations. The EBIT margin stood at 3.4%, supported by a 90-basis-point reduction in fulfilment costs.
Zalando reported a net loss of €18 million, compared with net income of €12.50 million a year earlier. Basic loss per share was €0.07, against a consensus forecast for earnings of €0.31 per share.

Mercedes-Benz Keeps Buying Back Stock While Analysts Trim Targets and China Strategy Awaits a Rewrit
sum: Mercedes-Benz is pressing ahead with its share buyback even after cutting its profit outlook, according to a fresh interim disclosure. The company repurchased 904,601 of its own shares last week, lifting the total since the programme began to 7,391,990. The filing confirms the buyback has continued uninterrupted since the profit warning issued just over a week ago.

The programme, announced on 31 August, covers up to 58 million shares and a volume of up to EUR 1 billion. It runs from 1 September through 6 April 2027, and the latest disclosure captures purchases completed by last Friday — a closed window inside a much longer schedule. That distinction matters: the reported figures show execution to date, while the announced caps define the ceiling. Nothing in the interim update points to a larger buyback or a faster pace.

The buybacks land against a deteriorating business outlook. In its profit warning, Mercedes-Benz cut the expected adjusted return on sales for Mercedes-Benz Cars for 2026 to 2–3%, down from a prior forecast of 3–5%. Management cited a tougher market environment in China and higher costs in the fourth quarter, including material costs.

Free cash flow from the industrial business is now expected well below the prior-year level, a downgrade from the earlier guidance of slightly below. Group EBIT is projected to merely match last year, having previously been expected to rise significantly. The buyback does nothing to ease these operating pressures and should be judged separately from the trajectory of the business.

The numbers published on Wednesday give ammunition to bulls and bears alike. Revenue in the third quarter of 2026 came in at EUR 30.7 billion, down from EUR 32.1 billion a year earlier. Group EBIT, by contrast, climbed to EUR 1.77 billion from EUR 0.75 billion, and net profit rose to EUR 1.52 billion from EUR 1.19 billion.

Volume and profit are therefore moving in opposite directions — a split that argues for looking at the two separately rather than reading the headline gain as a clean recovery. Nor do the stronger quarterly figures erase the burdens management has flagged for the rest of the year, which is why the annual EBIT guidance now points only to the prior-year level instead of a marked increase.

Jon Sumrall shares Tramell Jones injury news that sheds light on Florida QB situation
sum: Jon Sumrall's first-ever annual Florida-Georgia game went less than ideally, as Georgia's dominant defense spoiled any hopes of Sumrall's team pulling off an upset. The Gators fell 28-7 in a game that felt all-too-familiar to how the most recent iterations of the annual Florida-Georgia rivalry have gone.

One of the biggest storylines both before and during the game was Florida's quarterback situation. Coach Sumrall opted to start Aaron Philo under center, despite his back-up, Tramell Jones Jr., helping fuel Florida's upset over Texas two weeks prior. Philo was benched for Jones in the first half against Georgia after throwing two interceptions.

Even with the quarterback change, the offense didn't do much better, as Jones threw an interception of his own and finished with 172 yards passing with a garbage-time rushing touchdown late in the fourth quarter.
Jon Sumrall reveals Tramell Jones has an injury that could require surgery
After the game, Coach Sumrall revealed that Jones has been dealing with an injury that "may require surgery" at the end of the season. He did not disclose the specific nature of the injury.

"He's got an injury that may require surgery after the year," Sumrall told reporters. "Tramell really didn't look great with his health. I'm not going to tell y'all his injury because I'm not trying to help other people right now. But he's got a real injury, I think some people are questioning what's going on."

Both Jones and Philo were listed on Florida's injury report leading up to the Georgia game. Philo missed the Texas game due to a shoulder injury he suffered earlier in the season. Per Sumrall, Jones' injury paired with how Philo looked in practice before the Georgia game guided his decision on the starter.

Mercedes-Benz cuts 2026 outlook. Mercedes-Benz stock falls 5.05 percent
sum: Mercedes-Benz stock (ISIN DE0007100000) trades at EUR 39.28 at Lang & Schwarz on October 27, 2026, at 10:13 a.m. CET, down 5.05 percent versus the Xetra close of October 26, 2026, at EUR 41.37. Mercedes-Benz cut its 2026 outlook before publishing its third-quarter report. The update puts margin delivery ahead of the earnings release.

According to Der Aktionär, Mercedes-Benz Cars now expects an adjusted return on sales of 2 percent to 3 percent for 2026, compared with 3 percent to 5 percent previously. Group EBIT is now expected at the prior-year level instead of clearly above it, while industrial free cash flow is expected to be clearly below the prior year.

The preliminary third-quarter figures provide a mixed counterweight. Adjusted Cars return on sales was 2.5 percent against 2.4 percent consensus, while Group EBIT reached EUR 1.77 billion against EUR 1.60 billion consensus, according to the same October 27, 2026 release. Industrial free cash flow of EUR 172 million was below the EUR 422 million consensus.

The key issue is the gap between operating execution and the full-year cost outlook. A 2.5 percent Cars margin in the third quarter sits inside the new 2 percent to 3 percent range, but the lower ceiling leaves less room for higher material costs and weaker demand in China.

Mercedes-Benz had already shown softer volume trends before the outlook change. Simply Wall St reported that third-quarter 2026 sales reached 491,700 cars and vans, down 6 percent from a year earlier. That volume figure makes the revised margin range the central test for the full report.

The recent chronology runs from revenue of EUR 31.60 billion in the first quarter, reported on April 29, 2026, to EUR 32.06 billion in the second quarter, reported on July 28, 2026, and then to the October 27, 2026 outlook cut with third-quarter EBIT of EUR 1.77 billion. Investing.com lists the first-quarter and second-quarter revenue figures and their reporting dates.

The next two dated events are the third-quarter interim report and analyst conference call on October 28, 2026, followed by the sustainability update on November 10, 2026, according to Mercedes-Benz Group.

Rheinmetall's Customs Ship Contract Lifts Shares as Cash Flow Warning Clouds the Outlook
sum: Rheinmetall has secured a multi-year framework agreement to maintain and repair four liquefied natural gas-powered customs vessels, a deal that pushed the Düsseldorf defense contractor's stock higher on Wednesday even as broader concerns about its cash generation linger.

The shares advanced 2.5% to EUR 1,022.60 on the back of the naval service contract with Germany's General Customs Directorate. The gain builds on a modest 0.4% rise earlier in the session, when the stock was trading at EUR 1,002.00. Neither party disclosed the precise financial terms or delivery specifics, according to media reports.

For Rheinmetall's Naval Systems division, the award guarantees sustained maintenance work stretching across several years. The contract volume sits in the low single-digit millions of euros, with deliveries scheduled to run from late 2026 through the end of 2028.

The arrangement marks a strategic broadening of the company's customer base. While Rheinmetall's defense units primarily equip large military formations, the customs authority brings a federal agency focused on maritime surveillance and border security into the fold — an operational theater distinct from the group's traditional armed-forces business. The deal follows a string of other international naval and security contracts.

The maritime service win complements Rheinmetall's wider push into naval technology. On Monday, the company showcased networked unmanned systems designed to protect ports and critical infrastructure during the NATO exercise REPMUS26. The containerized solution is intended to serve the German Navy as a flexibly deployable mission system.

Beyond the naval sphere, Rheinmetall is expanding its vehicle-technology collaborations abroad. In the U.K., the company joined forces with Mercedes-Benz UK to present light tactical vehicles for the British Army, and it invested in a vibration testing facility at its Telford site for development of the Challenger 3 main battle tank.
The core defense business continues to generate substantial order intake. On September 14, Rheinmetall reported a major contract for 155-mm artillery ammunition from an international customer.

Volkswagen stock tumbles 7.5% on slashed profit guidance
sum: Investing.com -- Volkswagen AG (ETR:VOW) shares fell 7.5%, extending declines after the company cut its fiscal year 2026 operating return on sales guidance to up to 1%, down from a previous forecast of 4% to 5.5%.

The German automaker cited a goodwill impairment related to Porsche AG, a challenging market environment particularly in China, and additional restructuring expenses as reasons for the reduced outlook. The company now expects group sales revenue of around €315 billion, roughly equivalent to the midpoint of its previous forecast range.

Special effects totaling approximately €10 billion are expected to weigh on operating profit for the financial year, of which €0.9 billion were already reported in the first half of 2026. Adjusted for these special effects, the operating return on sales for the full year 2026 would amount to about 4%.

The forecast adjustment stems primarily from a deteriorating market environment, especially in China, and an accelerated shift in demand toward battery-electric vehicles. This has led to developments falling short of original expectations, particularly for the Audi and Volkswagen Passenger Cars brands.

Volkswagen will recognize a non-cash impairment of around €6 billion on goodwill allocated to the Porsche business segment in the third quarter. This follows updated medium- and long-term assumptions from Porsche AG regarding its enterprise value, including a medium-term corridor of 10% to 15%.

The company also expects additional restructuring expenses from expanded early retirement schemes and the planned sale of Volkswagen Osnabrück GmbH, connected to the "Future of Volkswagen" agreement reached at the end of 2024. Additionally, developments in the Chinese automotive market will lead to non-cash impairments of assets at fully consolidated companies in China. These three effects combined are expected to have a negative impact of around €2 billion in the second half of the year.
Volkswagen maintained its net cash flow guidance for the Automotive Division at €3 billion to €6 billion and net liquidity expectations at €32 billion to €34 billion for 2026.

sum: - Nio outsold Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi across eight provincial-level Chinese regions and 37 cities in August.
- The company has beaten the German luxury trio for six consecutive months in Guangdong and for two straight months in Jiangsu.
- The All-New ES8 sold 10,991 units in August, its 10th straight month above 10,000, and is approaching 150,000 cumulative deliveries.

U.S.-listed shares of Nio, Inc. (NIO) climbed 2% overnight late Thursday after the Chinese EV maker said it outsold Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi across eight provincial-level regions and 37 cities in August, driven by its premium SUVs.
Nio's U.S.-listed shares rose 1% on Thursday but remained down 2% for the week, putting the stock on track for its fourth consecutive weekly decline.

The figures, shared by Nio Assistant Vice President of User Operations Yang Bo, showed the company beating the German luxury trio — collectively known as BBA — in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shaanxi and Hainan, according to ChinaEVHome.

NIO sold 556 vehicles in Chongqing during August, moving ahead of Mercedes after previously surpassing Audi. It also overtook Mercedes in Shanxi for the first time after earlier passing BMW. The company has outsold all three German brands in Guangdong for six consecutive months and remained ahead of them in Jiangsu for a second straight month in August.

Mercedes-Benz Q2 2026 sales fall as China slump deepens
sum: China deliveries dropped 30% in the April-June period, even as battery-electric vehicle sales rose 50% globally

Mercedes-Benz reported on Wednesday that global car deliveries fell 8% in the second quarter compared with the same period a year earlier, with a deepening slump in China responsible for much of the decline. Across the quarter, the automaker handed over 417,800 vehicles to customers.

Chinese deliveries were down 30% from a year ago, a decline the automaker attributed to what it called "an intensifying competitive environment and the timing of the company's current product ramp-ups." Mercedes-Benz stock fell as much as 3.7% in Frankfurt trading.

Results outside China were considerably stronger. North America sales rose 13%, while European deliveries grew 4%. Fully electric models — counting both cars and vans — accounted for 63,000 deliveries, a 50% jump from the prior-year period, buoyed in part by European appetite for those vehicles. The automaker's highest-end lineup saw a 10% drop in deliveries, a result the company tied to scheduled transitions between model generations and when particular vehicles became available. Deliveries of the G-Class gained 3%.

Looking ahead to the back half of 2026, Mercedes-Benz plans to bring a number of China-specific vehicles to that market, among them the long-wheelbase electric GLC L SUV. Demand signals for the new S-Class are also encouraging in Europe, where the sedan's order books are described as strong through year-end.

The second-quarter results extend a pattern that has pressured the German automaker throughout 2026. In the first quarter, Mercedes-Benz reported a 6% global sales decline, with China down 27%, as domestic brands encroached on the premium segment. First-quarter earnings before interest and taxes fell 17% to €1.9 billion, and the carmaking unit's adjusted operating margin compressed to 4.1% from 7.3% a year earlier.

Across the German luxury segment, a prolonged real estate crisis in China has hollowed out the purchasing power of wealthier consumers, leaving brands like Mercedes, Porsche, and Audi disproportionately exposed as homegrown rivals press into the premium space. BMW last month warned that its automotive segment profit margin could fall as low as 1% due to weakness in China.

IT Stocks Swing From 52-Week Lows to a Rally as HCLTech Lands $1.14 Billion Mercedes Deal: Gold, Silver Rates Today
sum: India's IT stocks just lived through one of their wildest weeks in years. The Nifty IT index crashed to a 52-week low on June 30, kept falling on July 1, then staged its sharpest intraday rally since May 2025 on July 2, all before HCLTech announced a $1.14 billion deal that sent its shares soaring.

For anyone with money in IT stocks or in gold and silver, this is not background noise. It is the difference between panic-selling at the bottom and catching a genuine turnaround, right as Q1 FY27 earnings season opens and precious metal prices sit near record levels.

On June 30, the Nifty IT index sank to a 52-week low of 26,425.85, according to Business Standard. TCS touched ₹2,037 and Infosys fell to ₹1,005.50, both fresh lows. The index has now corrected nearly 42% from its all-time high of 46,089, hit back in December 2024.

The rout continued the next day. Business Today reported that Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL Technologies all hit fresh 52-week lows on July 1, as the Nifty IT sub-index fell another 2.01%. JPMorgan piled on by downgrading KPIT Technologies after it flagged a weaker June quarter tied to a slowdown among European automakers.

Then came the reversal. On July 2, the Sensex jumped 579.48 points, or 0.75%, to close at 77,502.12, while the Nifty50 rose 169.85 points to 24,175.70, per Business Standard. The Nifty IT index logged its best intraday gains since May 2025, with Infosys, Tech Mahindra and TCS leading the Nifty50's gainers.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, said the broader market rose as easing tensions around the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude prices lower, while dovish comments from the US Fed Chair reinforced expectations of cooling inflation.

The real jolt for IT stocks landed on July 3. HCLTech told stock exchanges it had signed a $1.14 billion agreement, reported by sources to be with Mercedes-Benz, to build and run an AI-driven operating model for the client's global digital workplace and enterprise network infrastructure, according to Kotak Neo. The contract runs from July 2026 to December 2031, with an option to extend by five more years.
